pages.title: The circulation as a closed route
pages.text:
The circulation as a closed route
left heart → systemic bed → right heart ,
right heart → pulmonary bed → left heart .
A route speciﬁes connections. It does not yet determine the ﬂow on any connection.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 2 / 20

pages.title: Chambers, valves, and vascular beds
pages.text:
Chambers, valves, and vascular beds
The pulmonary and systemic beds are in series.
Within a bed, individual vessels branch and rejoin.
Arteries and veins are named by direction relative to the heart, not by oxygen content.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 4 / 20

pages.text:
Sign and limiting cases
∆P = 0 ⇒ Q = 0.
∆P < 0 ⇒ Q < 0 ( R > 0).
A one-way valve requires an extra rule; a signed resistance alone does not enforce one-way
ﬂow.

pages.title: Instantaneous flow and cycle average
pages.text:
Instantaneous ﬂow and cycle average
A chamber may store blood during part of a beat.
If its volume returns to its starting value after one complete cycle,
volume entering per cycle = volume leaving per cycle .
This is an average constraint, not equality at every instant.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 18 / 20

pages.title: From one element to a circulation
pages.text:
From one element to a circulation
The resistance calculation determines Q from prescribed pressures.
A closed circulation must also determine those pressures from pumping, storage, and
conservation.
The next construction adds an elastic reservoir.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 20 / 20
